record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a bound for the number of balanced vertices of any finite connected embedded geodesic net in the Euclidean plane that depends only on the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance, where the imbalance vector at an unbalanced vertex is the sum of all outgoing unit tangent vectors along incident edges and the total imbalance is the sum of the norms of these imbalance vectors over all unbalanced vertices?

evidence.quote: We call this sum the imbalance vector Imb(v) at v, and its norm the imbalance, imb(v), at v. The sum of imbalances v∈S imb(v) over the set of all unbalanced points is called the total imbalance of the geodesic net.
Conjecture 3.4.1 (M. Gromov). The number of balanced vertices of a geodesic net in the Euclidean plane can be bounded above in terms of the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite connected graph embedded in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight line segments (a finite connected embedded geodesic net). For each vertex $v$ of $\Gamma$, define the imbalance vector
$$\mathrm{Imb}(v) = \sum_{e \ni v} \mathbf{u}_{v,e},$$
where the sum runs over all edges $e$ incident to $v$, and $\mathbf{u}_{v,e}$ denotes the unit tangent vector at $v$ pointing along $e$ away from $v$. Call $v$ balanced if $\mathrm{Imb}(v) = 0$ and unbalanced otherwise. The imbalance at $v$ is $\mathrm{imb}(v) = \|\mathrm{Imb}(v)\|$, and the total imbalance of $\Gamma$ is
$$T(\Gamma) = \sum_{v \text{ unbalanced}} \mathrm{imb}(v).$$
Let $U(\Gamma)$ denote the number of unbalanced vertices and $B(\Gamma)$ the number of balanced vertices.

Question: Does there exist a function $F : \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ such that for every finite connected embedded geodesic net $\Gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$,
$$B(\Gamma) \leq F(U(\Gamma),\, T(\Gamma))?$$
artifact.category_tag: Geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to M. Gromov, asks whether the number of balanced vertices in a planar geodesic net can be bounded in terms of the number of unbalanced vertices plus the total imbalance. Recent work (2024–2025) on geodesic nets with few boundary (unbalanced) vertices reports progress on related variants but does not establish such a bound; constructions producing many balanced vertices with four boundary vertices suggest the bare unbalanced-vertex version may fail, while the version with total imbalance included remains open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: increases the previously known maximum for balanced vertices of nets with four boundary vertices from 16 to 25
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on bounding balanced vertices indicates the problem remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: there is a different conjecture that it is possible to bound the number of balanced vertices in terms of the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance
status_evidence.claim: The total-imbalance bound conjecture is stated as still conjectural in recent literature.
